title: windowed-relocation allocator for KV cache to minimize tail fragmentation and preserve large contiguous GPU blocks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under mixed workloads (a blend of short-chat interactions and infrequent long-context generations) our current KV allocation strategy scatters variable-length token entries across many small free gaps, creating tail fragmentation that prevents allocating new long-context requests without evicting many unrelated prefixes. This increases evictions, causes SLO regressions for tail-latency requests, and raises token cost due to extra recomputation.

Proposed solution: Implement a "windowed-relocation allocator" that maintains multiple allocation arenas by age and density and performs bounded background relocation within a sliding time window. Key ideas:
- Hot/Cold separation: allocate new KV entries preferentially from a "recent" arena tuned for frequent churn and smaller allocations; longer-lived contexts are placed in a "stable" arena optimized for larger contiguous chunks.
- Windowed relocation: periodically scan a limited range of arenas and coalesce adjacent free slots by relocating resident entries into compacted regions. Relocation is bounded (max bytes moved per GPU per second) to respect latency SLOs.
- Size classes + split/coalesce policy: use coarse-grained size classes to reduce metadata overhead, with opportunistic splitting when a large free block is required for a long-context request.
- Allocation affinity: try to allocate tokens for the same request/session onto adjacent slots (sticky allocation) to maximize prefix locality for KV cache reuse.
- Fallback eviction: when contiguity still can't be satisfied, trigger an eviction policy preferring entries with low reuse score and older age in the recent arena.

Why different from existing allocators: instead of global compaction or frequent full defrag, this design uses a bounded, time-windowed relocation with arena separation and affinity heuristics to reduce IO and avoid SLO impact during compaction. It focuses on preserving large contiguous blocks for tail requests while keeping churn cheap for common short requests.

Success metrics and signals:
- 75% reduction in fragmentation-induced request failures for >8k token allocations on p4/p8 (measured by inability to allocate contiguous KV across existing free slabs).
- <5% added token-latency variance from relocation background work (measured as p95 latency delta vs baseline under mixed workload).
- Net decrease in eviction rate for long-context requests by >=40%.
- Controlled background memory copy bandwidth: configurable cap (default 20 MB/s per GPU).

Implementation plan:
1) Design: (this ticket) finalize arena boundaries, relocation window size, and size-class granularity. Draft design doc and benchmarks. (Owner: Lena)
2) Instrumentation: extend KV metadata to include arena id, last-access timestamp, and reuse score. Add metrics for fragmentation, contiguous-free-block histogram, and background-move bandwidth. (Owner: infra)
3) Runtime allocator: implement arena allocation and sticky-affinity heuristics in the runtime allocation path; keep fast-path allocation non-blocking. (Owner: serving-runtime)
4) Background relocator: single-threaded relocator per GPU with throttling, checkpointing and graceful backoff when SDK requests spike. (Owner: serving-runtime)
5) Testing & Benchmarks: microbenchmarks for allocation latency, relocator overhead; system tests with mixed-sequence synthetic workload; end-to-end perf on canary cluster. (Owner: perf-team)
6) Rollout: feature gate behind runtime flag + canary 5% traffic, then 25% then 100% if metrics look good. Add automatic disable if relocation bandwidth causes p99 latency regressions.

Rollout/Op plan:
- Default off for existing dedicated customers. Enable in a controlled canary and surface config knobs in Redwood Console under Runtime -> Memory Optimization.
- Provide tuning presets: "balanced" (default), "throughput-first" (lower relocation bandwidth), "latency-first" (aggressive separation of arenas, minimal relocation).

Backward compatibility and migration:
- On upgrade, new allocator will be enabled in passive mode to collect fragmentation metrics without moving data. After a short observation period, enable relocation with conservative defaults.
- Provide a dry-run mode that simulates relocation decisions and logs predicted gains.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How to set arena cut points for different GPUs (A100 vs H100) and quantized vs fp16 KV entries? Plan: initial heuristics based on typical sequence-length percentiles from telemetry; allow per-cluster tuning.
- Relocation cost vs benefit: need to tune bytes/sec cap to avoid interfering with inference bandwidth. We'll use adaptive throttling tied to request queue depth.
- Metadata overhead: adding a few bytes per KV entry increases memory. We will evaluate a compact metadata layout and consider sampling to reduce overhead.

Dependencies:
- Continuous batching improvements (ENG-20210) for accurate sequence-length distribution signals.
- KV eviction scoring refinement (ENG-19322) to prefer low-reuse entries for relocation targets.

Business/customer impact:
- Medium to high for customers using long-context features (e.g., retrieval-augmented generation, long-document chat). Reduces failed long-context requests and lowers overall cost by avoiding unnecessary evictions and recompute.

Monitoring & alerts:
- New dashboards: contiguous-free-blocks by GPU, active relocation bandwidth, relocation-induced latency delta, arena utilization heatmap.
- Alert if background move bandwidth > configured cap for >5 minutes or if p99 latency increases >10% on canary rollout.

Dependencies/Follow-ups:
- Follow-up ticket to add GPU-aware relocation heuristics for multi-tenant nodes (share relocation budget across customers).
- Integration with Optimize recommendations to suggest arena presets per workload.
